findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Realign unit 2 to the parent epic's contract: the authoritative `multi-project-bridge` stamp is the `bridge projects` set/remove write path landing the stamp + mapping mutation in ONE tracker commit (owned by the store-compat child), with this ensure unit positioned only as a convergence backstop — and drop the 'single authoritative stamp' / 'no sibling owns a write-time stamp' claims that contradict the epic's final AC.
evidence: Parent epic 0e68-41eb decomposition: the mapping-store child 'Delivers the migration and legacy-default criteria' (i.e. seed + legacy default), while a SEPARATE child 'The store-compat capability stamp ... Delivers the final criterion.'

Parent epic (condensed decomposition): 'the `bridge projects` set/remove write path writes the re-derived stamp and the mapping mutation in the SAME tracker commit (one atomic publish ...)' and 'the atomic-commit writer is the only path that can make a store multi-project' and 'Ensure sweeps are convergence backstops for any residual divergence, not the trigger.'

Parent epic final AC: 'A store whose mapping holds more than one project carries multi-project-bridge in .store-compat.json required_capabilities ... including that the stamp and mapping mutation land in one tracker commit (asserted on the commit's tree).'

Leaf Approach: 'No sibling owns a write-time stamp (7032 only documents the token), so this ensure unit is the single authoritative stamp' and 'it fires on a later sweep once an operator added a second project' — a sweep-triggered ensure unit, not the parent's atomic write-time set/remove commit.
The leaf's stamp unit cannot satisfy the parent's 'land in one tracker commit' AC because it stamps on a subsequent sweep, decoupled from the mapping mutation.
findings.finding: The leaf redefines the capability-stamp deliverable that the parent epic assigns to a DISTINCT sibling child and specifies as an atomic write-time commit, contradicting a parent acceptance criterion.
scenarios: An operator runs `bridge projects set` to add a second project: the epic requires the stamp+mapping to publish atomically in one commit on that write; the leaf instead leaves the store unstamped until a later init/fsck/MCP-boot sweep converges it, leaving an observable window where a multi-project store is unstamped.
The store-compat child (milksnake) and this leaf both claim ownership of the authoritative stamp, contradicting the epic's disjoint-file, single-owner decomposition.
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe unit 2 as an explicit convergence backstop that re-derives the stamp from the mapping when it diverges (matching the epic's 'Ensure sweeps are convergence backstops ... not the trigger'), and defer authoritative-stamp ownership + the one-commit AC to the store-compat sibling child rather than asserting no sibling owns a write-time stamp.
